entry.label: Feedforward
entry.description: Anticipatory action based on a desired future, a measured disturbance or a model of likely effects, taken before the resulting output is available for correction.
entry.canonical_definition: A control or coordination relation in which information about intended conditions or measured disturbances is used to act before the resulting output is observed; effectiveness depends on the adequacy of the model or prediction.

profile.title: Feedforward
profile.canonical_definition: A control or coordination relation in which information about intended conditions or measured disturbances is used to act before the resulting output is observed; effectiveness depends on the adequacy of the model or prediction.
profile.summary: Feedforward acts before the result is available to be measured. It uses intention, forecast or measured disturbance to shape action in advance. It is usually strongest when combined with feedback that corrects modelling error and surprise.
profile.why_it_matters: Waiting for failure before responding is often costly. Feedforward can prepare capacity, prevent deviation and make intentions interpretable. Its weakness is that it depends on the quality of the model, forecast and disturbance sensing.
key_distinctions: anticipatory action vs reaction to output
historical_lineage: anticipatory control developed alongside feedback control
the term also developed a communication meaning in cybernetic discussions
modern engineering commonly combines feedforward with feedback
logical_antecedents: a model or expectation of effects
capacity to act before output changes
practice_connections: ask what can be known early enough to matter
state the assumptions in the predictive model
open_checks: I. A. Richards and Macy lineage
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.

connections.notes: Feedforward anticipates disturbances; feedback responds to observed consequences. They are often combined.

claims.statement: Feedforward acts before output error is observed and therefore depends on adequate disturbance measurement, forecasting or a model of likely effects.
claims.notes: The object is a placeholder for informational/model dependence, not a claim that Shannon information theory is always required.
